messages:
marta: Quick follow-up to the ABI minimization RFC. Proposal: implement a small feature-negotiator protocol instead of always shipping full manifests to every runtime. Control-plane would emit a compact capability vector + negotiator version; runtimes interpret locally. Pros: much smaller payloads, quicker fallback decisions, simpler deltas for private deployments. Cons: more logic moves into adapters which increases surface for divergence.
kevin: I like the reduced payloads. Major question: secrets and KMS access. If adapters make local decisions based on capability bits, they might need to fetch keys or assert identity to external KMS. Where does that responsibility sit?
sam: agree on the key issue. Also telemetry: when adapters alter behavior by capability we must surface that for model-quality/regression alerts. If we don't, teams will optimize for token cost and regress answer quality silently.
marta: design thought: capability vector = small bitmask + optional metadata URL for richer cases. Auth remains control-plane-led: control-plane issues a short-lived signed claim scoped to capabilities (very short TTL). That claim is validated locally; adapter then fetches any extra secrets from customer KMS only when strictly necessary.
alex: need a canonical compatibility fallback. If negotiator version mismatch or validation fails, runtime should fall back to the legacy full-manifest (compat v0) path so we have safe rollbacks.
kevin: fallback doubles attack surface unless we ensure the fallback enforces identical auth/policy checks. Rate-limits and quota enforcement must be preserved.
marta: agreed. Encode policy_id into the claim so adapter enforces same quotas and checks across both flows.
sam: telemetry notes: include capability vector and negotiator path in traces and per-route metrics. Add two tags: redwood.capvec and redwood.negotiator.path. Also add a rollout lineage id to correlate regressions back to a rollout.
kevin: private deployments: they might not accept signed claims from our control-plane. Options: (A) pre-shared signing keys / PKI bootstrap to let their control-plane sign claims, (B) keep the full-manifest path for private only. PKI adds onboarding complexity but converges UX long-term.
alex: long-term we should converge. My vote is PKI bootstrap + explicit rotation steps during onboarding. Short-term: gate private to legacy manifests until bootstrap UX shipped.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: negotiator v1 canary -> staging 2025-10-12T22:00Z. Production tentative after perf + security reviews.
sam: perf hypothesis: vector+embedded-token reduces payload and parsing cost vs full JSON manifest; bigger wins from fewer secret fetch roundtrips. Bench matrix: (1) full-manifest (legacy), (2) vector+embedded-token (hosted fast path), (3) vector+ref-token + local-KMS (private-like).
kevin: define handshake SLO. Simulate failure modes: missing token, expired token, PKI mismatch. Goal: negotiation handshake <15ms median on target infra.
alex: ops controls: tenant-level feature-flag to force compatibility-manifest path so SRE can flip if anomalies appear. Also add per-tenant observability to detect which path used.
marta: tentative capability vector sketch (debug text form):

ver:1
bits: "GEN_CHAT|EMBED|CACHE_PREFIX|LOW_LATENCY"
policy_id: "billing-v2"
sig: "<signed-claim-or-ref>"

Notes: human-readable for debugging; wire format will be compact binary bitfield. Decision points: sig embedded vs referenced. Embedded reduces roundtrips (nice for hosted) but increases token size. Reference reduces size but requires 1 fetch. Suggest: embedded for hosted/dedicated, reference allowed for private/airgapped.

sam: make sure traces expose embed vs ref path so we can correlate fetch latencies. Also add an 'adapter-ver' tag to traces to detect divergence across adapter versions.
kevin: security: add a review milestone for PKI bootstrap. Also ensure fallback path enforces same policy-id checks and does not relax auth.
alex: plan: prototype in 2 sprints, then staging canary mid-next-cycle. I'll create engineering tickets for tenant-flag, fallback, and rollout tests.
marta: action items: 1) sam - prototype trace tagging + bench plan. 2) kevin - token/claim schema + PKI bootstrap proposal. 3) alex - tenant feature flag + manifest fallback toggle. 4) marta - docs + private onboarding notes. I'll draft an RFC addendum consolidating these. Please put scope and rollback details in your tickets. :thumbsup:
